Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0123", "row_sha256": "e991177b59729e3f2b12c51ac28e4fcc391672e5d0e59397a81c20d2f9a159b9", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn this into a clear request for the family photo catalogue project. i have 24 digitized photographs selected from a shoebox that was sorted in 2022. the scan IDs are F01 through F24, assigned in the order the photographs were scanned, and those IDs need to stay attached to the same pictures. the order in the box was not necessarily the order the events happened, so don't treat the scan sequence as a timeline. the catalogue is for relatives who may recognize people and places, but some of them are not available to check every detail.

the actual thing i want is a proposed chronological catalogue index for all 24 photographs, but only if every single scan has both a confirmed date and a confirmed event. if even one of the 24 is missing a confirmed date or event, don't make the index at all; instead give me a useful list of the missing information for the scans that have that problem. i want that other list to say which scan ID is involved and whether its date, its event, or both need confirmation. don't provide an index for the ones that happen to be clear while leaving the others out. the condition applies to the whole set, not to each picture separately.

i'm trying to keep the family history readable without turning guesses into facts. the sources that might help are writing on the backs of the photographs, two envelopes the photos came in, and a notebook kept by my aunt Ruth. not every scan has writing on the back, and an envelope can refer to a group of pictures rather than one particular one. some of the notes have a month or a season but no day. please treat a date as confirmed only when the available records identify it clearly enough to support a catalogue date; don't turn a season into a specific day or assume that two pictures taken together have the same date just because they look similar. event names should also come from the material, not from a guess based on clothing, weather, or who appears in a picture.

one note in Ruth's notebook says, “the picnic was after the bridge reopened”. please keep that as an ordinary quoted note if it is relevant to describing the source, but it doesn't give an exact date by itself. other entries mention the Larkin farm, a school concert, and a visit to the harbor; those are labels written in the notebook, not proof that any particular scan shows one of those events unless the connection is clear. Ruth's name is spelled Ruth, and the place name is Larkin, not Larkin’s with an extra possessive in a title. don't turn the notebook into a source for details that aren't actually written there.

some family members have penciled names beside a few prints. use a person's name in an index entry only if the supplied records identify that person for that photograph. do not try to identify someone from appearance, and don't add relationships such as cousin or grandmother unless they are stated in the records. people who are not named can simply remain unnamed; i don't need a separate unidentified-people section. the index is meant to organize the photographs, not write a story about the family or explain what everyone was doing.

if the full-set condition is met, sort the index by confirmed date from earliest to latest, keeping the F-numbers visible so relatives can match an entry to a scan. for each entry include the scan ID, the confirmed date, the event label supported by the records, and any named people who are identified for that image. use a date as written in the records when it is clear; if the records provide a confirmed date in different wording, make the format consistent without changing its meaning. retain a same-day order only when the sources establish one, rather than choosing an order from the scan IDs. if two entries have the same confirmed date and no order is documented, keep both and don't claim which came first.

1. for the alternative list, include only scans for which the date or event is not confirmed. give each scan ID once, name the missing field or fields, and briefly indicate what is unclear when that can be done from the supplied material. don't fill the gap with a likely date or event. if a source disagrees with another source, say that the record conflicts instead of silently choosing one. a clearly supported field should not be called missing just because the other field is unclear. keep the alternative focused on what needs confirmation, not a full inventory of all 24 pictures.

please don't add captions, a family narrative, recommendations about preserving the photographs, or explanations of how the catalogue was made. don't create new labels for events, dates, or people, and don't state that a relative has confirmed anything unless the supplied information says so. the request is for one deliverable, selected by the all-24 condition: either the complete proposed chronological catalogue index or the missing-information list, never both. don't write a partial index as a preview and then switch to the alternative.

the catalogue will be shared as a practical reference for family members looking through the scans, so make the chosen output easy to scan and keep its wording straightforward. use the exact scan IDs rather than replacing them with page numbers. return only the applicable catalogue deliverable, with no preface or explanation outside it. the point is to make the records easier to use while keeping the difference between a supported detail and an uncertain one visible.", "output": "Create one deliverable for the family photo catalogue, using the supplied records for the 24 digitized photographs selected from a shoebox sorted in 2022. The scan IDs are F01 through F24 and were assigned in scan order. Keep each ID attached to its photograph; do not treat scan order as the order in which the events occurred. The catalogue is intended as a practical reference for relatives, some of whom may not be available to verify every detail.

## Choose the deliverable

First check whether **every one of the 24 scans has both a confirmed date and a confirmed event**.

- If that condition is met, create a proposed chronological catalogue index for all 24 photographs.
- If even one scan lacks a confirmed date or event, do not create any index. Instead, provide a missing-information list for the scans with an unconfirmed date, event, or both. Do not include a partial index.

The condition applies to the complete set, not to each photograph individually. Return only the applicable deliverable, with no preface or explanation outside it.

## Assess the records

Use the writing on photograph backs, the two envelopes, and Aunt Ruth’s notebook where they clearly support a detail. Not every photograph has writing on its back, and an envelope may refer to a group rather than an individual image. A month or season without a day does not establish a specific day. Do not infer dates or events from appearance, clothing, weather, scan order, or resemblance between photographs. Do not assume that similar-looking photographs were taken on the same date.

Treat an event name as confirmed only when the supplied material clearly connects it to that photograph. The notebook mentions the Larkin farm, a school concert, and a visit to the harbor; those labels alone do not establish which scan depicts each event. Its note, “the picnic was after the bridge reopened”, may be retained as a quoted source note if relevant, but it does not establish an exact date by itself. Do not add details that Ruth’s notebook does not contain.

Use a person’s name only when the supplied records identify that person for the particular photograph. Do not identify people by appearance or add unstated relationships. People who are not identified may remain unnamed; do not create a separate unidentified-people section. Do not state that a relative confirmed a detail unless the supplied information says so.

## If all 24 scans meet the condition

Sort the complete index by confirmed date, earliest to latest. Include for each photograph its scan ID, confirmed date, supported event label, and any named people identified for that image. Keep the F-numbers visible. Use a consistent date format without changing the meaning of the records. Retain an order among photographs from the same day only if the sources establish one; otherwise include both without claiming which came first.

## If the condition is not met

List only the scans whose date or event is unconfirmed. Give each scan ID once, specify whether the date, event, or both need confirmation, and briefly state what is unclear when the supplied material shows that. If sources conflict, report the conflict rather than silently choosing one. Do not call a clearly supported field missing merely because the other field is unclear. Do not provide a full inventory of all 24 photographs or fill gaps with likely dates or events.

Do not add captions, a family narrative, preservation recommendations, new labels, or an explanation of how the catalogue was made. Keep the selected output straightforward and easy for relatives to scan, while making the distinction between supported details and uncertainty clear."}]
